project.name: research
project.description: Thesis scaffold for an agentic AI system that analyzes observability data, identifies root causes, and recommends remediation in a Docker Compose Online Boutique SRE environment. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project purpose and architecture
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the thesis goal: an agent that investigates faults and recommends controlled remediation in a simulated SRE environment. The architecture document explains why the research deployment uses its own Docker Compose stack while keeping Online Boutique source as upstream reference material.

tour.title: The simulated environment and telemetry stack
tour.description: Building on the system boundaries from Step 1, the Compose definition describes the application and observability services that form the experiment environment. Prometheus configuration shows how telemetry is collected, giving the agent evidence to inspect during an incident.

tour.title: Experiment runtime and shared settings
tour.description: The research CLI exposes environment checks, snapshots, and fault-run workflows, while the Compose adapter provides controlled access to service state and allowlisted operations. Shared configuration centralizes research paths, telemetry endpoints, and runtime controls used by these components.

tour.title: Collecting incident evidence
tour.description: The read-only observer gathers Prometheus, Loki, alert, and Jaeger data for an experiment window. This evidence path connects the simulated environment to the RCA agent, while keeping telemetry access separate from actions that can change service state.

tour.title: Defining controlled faults and ground truth
tour.description: The fault generator validates scenario inputs, and a scenario file describes a concrete packet-loss experiment, including the target service and expected evidence. The fault-injection guide explains the execution gates and ground-truth artifacts that make experiments repeatable and evaluable.

tour.title: How an RCA session starts and runs
tour.description: The agent command-line entry point hands a session to the run coordinator, which then drives the AIOpsLab-compatible loop for setup, interaction, evaluation, and cleanup. Following these files shows how the agent layer consumes the runtime and telemetry capabilities introduced earlier.

tour.title: Bounded reasoning and model providers
tour.description: The strategy controller validates actions, manages incident budgets, and caches short-lived queries so an RCA session stays bounded. Provider implementations supply either deterministic test responses or OpenAI-compatible chat, while sanitization removes sensitive or withheld fields before evidence reaches the agent.

tour.title: Evaluating diagnoses and semantic fault evidence
tour.description: Evaluation modules compare the agent's diagnosis with experiment ground truth, and semantic probes check whether injected code-level faults produce the intended behavior. These pieces connect controlled fault construction to measurable RCA outcomes rather than relying only on whether a run completed.

tour.title: The research dashboard
tour.description: The FastAPI application exposes scenario, job, and experiment-result routes, while the job manager coordinates GUI runs and reports sanitized status. The static HTML shell presents scenario selection, active jobs, and history, providing a user-facing path into the same research workflows.

tour.title: Recording experiment results
tour.description: The artifact helpers create experiment identifiers and write versioned JSON plus append-only event records, preserving the evidence needed for later analysis. The experiment log template ties those outputs back to a documented record of setup, observations, and evaluation results.
